title: How do we build a big square from shaded small squares?
description: A big square is built from equal small squares, using perpendicular grid lines, diagonals and parallel shading. A plain two by two block is left in one corner.
teaching_notes: One idea: when a big square is made of equal small squares, choosing the small side first fixes every other length. Watch for students who shade a different triangle in each small square.

video_script.why: A learner builds a big square from equal small squares, draws diagonals in them and shades the same triangle in each.
video_script.substitution: the same way as the example in your book: squares drawn with perpendicular sides and diagonals
video_script.anchor: a big square made of equal small squares, some halved by diagonals and shaded, with one plain larger square in a corner
video_script.payoff_line: Every small square carries the same shaded triangle.

final_answer.value: Open ended. A big square of equal small squares, with diagonals, the same triangle of each shaded, and one plain larger square covering a 2 by 2 block

maths_rules: the measurements are our choice, so let each small square have side 1 cm
a big square of side 4 cm holds 4 small squares along each side, 4 times 4 = 16 small squares
a diagonal splits a small square into two equal triangles, and the same triangle is shaded in each
the plain larger square covers a 2 by 2 block of small squares, side 2 cm
video_script.design: The small side is chosen, the grid is drawn, then the diagonals and the shading follow, and a corner block is left plain.
open_questions: The exact picture of Construct 3 is not in the book text, so the figure follows the worklist wording: a 4 by 4 grid with one plain 2 by 2 corner block.
